method: Public official engineering publications, named firsthand interviews, vendor publications and author-linked research repositories. Opened and read relevant text; no private access, contact, installations or production probes. Source count is not a count of independently verified deployments. Summaries paraphrase bounded claims; no long quotations.

sources.title: American Express adopts NVIDIA AI for fraud prevention — official Japanese edition
sources.scope: Amex global card-transaction fraud; Japanese translation of vendor case, not Japan-only product availability
sources.evidence: Names Manish Gupta. Describes TensorFlow/DGX training and TensorRT/Triton/T4 serving with recurrent LSTM plus GBM; subsystem latency requirement and segment-specific improvement claims.
sources.limitations: T02 names GRU instead. Exact variant unresolved; historical vendor claims, no independent benchmark or current topology. Japanese currency translation is unreliable and not reused.
sources.access: Full relevant Japanese text opened. English original redirects to a tag archive; Taiwan official translation also opened.

sources.title: Simplifying and Scaling Inference Serving with NVIDIA Triton 2.3
sources.scope: Amex-specific customer subsection of a general NVIDIA technical article
sources.evidence: Amex subsection specifies a TensorRT-optimized GRU served by Triton on T4-equipped servers within a 2 ms fraud budget.
sources.limitations: Model label conflicts with T01. General product architecture, Kubernetes and Azure sections do not establish Amex deployment; no end-to-end authorization SLA.
sources.access: Full customer subsection read; AI-generated page summary was not used as evidence.

sources.title: Available Now: NVIDIA AI Accelerated DGL and PyG Containers for GNNs
sources.scope: Amex AI Labs graph-based fraud research
sources.evidence: Coauthor Alireza Zaheri identified as Amex AI Labs director. Amex section describes DGL experiments using multi-node/multi-GPU infrastructure with millions of nodes and billions of edges.
sources.limitations: No Amex production GNN deployment or graph database is named. Other benchmarks and PyG customer results must not be attributed to Amex.
sources.access: Full Amex subsection and author bio read; ignored generated summary.

sources.title: A New Method for Enhancing Neural Network Training
sources.scope: Amex Global Decision Science researchers and Imperial College collaboration
sources.evidence: Authors Leonie Goldmann and Marcus September describe adaptive preprocessing of irregular financial series and four sequential sublayers, linking the EDAIN paper.
sources.limitations: No live deployment stated. Missing-value handling and broader risk applications remain research directions. Not evidence of underwriting rules.
sources.access: Full text and figure captions read; direct diagram image fetch failed.

sources.title: Extended Deep Adaptive Input Normalization for Preprocessing Time Series Data for Neural Networks
sources.scope: AISTATS 2024 paper; Imperial and Amex Decision Science coauthors
sources.evidence: Defines EDAIN/EDAIN-KL, global/local variants, evaluation methods and experimental configurations; links author implementation.
sources.limitations: First submission 2023-10-23. Algorithm and benchmark disclosures do not expose live card authorization architecture, customer policies or production risk weights. Paper CC-BY does not license every code/data asset.
sources.access: Abstract, full HTML method, affiliations and relevant experimental/reference sections read.

sources.title: marcusGH/edain_paper research implementation
sources.scope: Author-owned research repository linked by T05; not an Amex-organization repository
sources.status: public implementation, not installed or evaluated
sources.evidence: README provides PyTorch implementation/reproduction guidance and documents possible NaN gradients. License section identifies differing third-party asset terms and specific research dataset permission.
sources.limitations: Amex connection is paper lineage, not company repository ownership. No blanket license verified from inspected root/README. No dataset downloaded; this research does not authorize its use.
sources.access: Repository root, README, known issues and license-information section read. Source execution and dependency audit not performed.

sources.title: americanexpress/rate-limiting-scheduled-executor
sources.status: public implementation, production workload not named
sources.evidence: Per-executor throughput controls, Redis peer discovery, interval/overflow buckets, timeout filtering and caller-provided executor described; Apache-2.0 declared.
sources.limitations: Timing may precede or exceed scheduled time. No durable financial-workflow guarantee, current support assurance or payment-system adoption claim. Not a TypeScript drop-in.
sources.access: README architecture steps and limitations read. Linked diagram image fetch failed; no code execution or benchmark replication.

sources.evidence: Hadoop integrated with analytics/operations; controlled data access, self-service Labs/APIs/algorithm libraries, incremental expansion and retained relational workloads described.

sources.access: Complete Q&A read; secondary conference reporting not used for quantitative claims.
